attributes.morphology: gully like lines and surface fractals

evidence.quote: There were some gully like lines and surface fractals (dashed ellipse in Fig. 2e1) on the surface of the Cu–12Cr–6Nb powder indicating the poor fluidity.
Cu–1Cr–0.5Nb exhibited the smallest angle of repose at 22°, indicating superior fluidity.
Cu–12Cr–6Nb powder displayed a stacking angle of 35°, indicating reduced fluidity compared to Cu–1Cr–0.5Nb.
with the addition of 1 at.% Cr and 0.5 at.% Nb to pure Cu, a notable decrease of 14.9% in laser reflectance was observed.
the extent of improvement in laser absorption rate diminished as the composition transition from Cu–8Cr–4Nb to Cu–12Cr–6Nb, where only a 3.8% enhancement in laser absorption rate was obtained.
Cu–12Cr–6Nb showed a relatively poor fluidity

mechanisms.name: laser absorption enhancement by Cr/Nb surface coverage

evidence.quote: the adherence of Cr and Nb to the Cu particle surface effectively diminished the uncoated Cu surface area, resulting in reduced overall laser reflectivity for Cu.
